messages:
ana: Heads-up — our Okta alert flagged a mass MFA push pattern for bryan@redwood.com, ~120 push attempts in the last 30m from a cluster of foreign IPs. Alert name: suspicious-mfa-flood.
jamal: Copy. Are any of those attempts succeeding? pulling logs now.
ana: okta-bot posted a summary (pasted): IPs 185.48.93.12, 46.101.45.9, 51.15.22.7. Locations vary. No successful auth seen yet; lots of push declines/no-response.
maria: MFA fatigue attack — even without success we should treat as active compromise attempt. Recommend suspend and revoke.
devsec: Agreed. Proposed immediate actions: suspend user in Okta, revoke all sessions and refresh tokens, force password reset, block offending IPs at WAF, and check KMS/CloudTrail for any key usage tied to the account. Who's oncall?
liyah: oncall here. I'll take WAF blocks and Okta actions. Doing suspend now.
oncall-bot: /okta suspend bryan@redwood.com — success (OKTA-API-200).
sre-bot: WAF rule deployed: block ip set {185.48.93.12,46.101.45.9,51.15.22.7} — propagation to edge in ~60s.
jamal: Pulling session ids. If we can, revoke refresh tokens for all active sessions and rotate any long-lived service tokens the user owns.
nana: Okta API call I used: 
```
curl -X POST "https://api.okta.com/api/v1/users/bryan@redwood.com/lifecycle/suspend"\
  -H "Authorization: SSWS $OKTA_TOKEN"
```
no success events for primary apps but there are many token-exchange attempts to the OAuth token endpoint originating from the same IPs.
maria: Checking CloudTrail/KMS: no unusual KMS Decrypt/Encrypt calls from those IPs. Looks limited to Okta/OAuth attempts. Still, rotate any service tokens that might have been cached on the user's machine if they used CLI keys.
devsec: Good catch. Action: list all service principals owned by bryan, mark for rotation, and add to incident ticket. Also add a detection rule to flag >10 push attempts to a single account in 15m.
jamal: I pushed a SIEM rule now and added a temporary throttling policy in Okta for push notifications to that account. Also blacklisted the IPs at cloud edge.
liyah: User contacted support and confirmed they did not approve any prompts. They've been advised to check devices and reset password. We'll escalate to account recovery flow if anything looks off.
maria: Creating follow-up tasks: #INC-1892 create Okta global push-rate policy; #INC-1893 KMS audit rule for principal-initiated decrypts; #INC-1894 update runbook for MFA fatigue. I'll own #INC-1892.
devsec: Post-incident checklist we should do in next 48h: 1) Add throttling/rate limits at the IdP, 2) enforce per-user push caps, 3) update runbook and train SOC, 4) add SIEM enrichment for IP cluster detection, 5) review RBAC list to ensure no overly permissive tokens tied to user.
jamal: Noted — I'll open a PR for runbook updates and add steps to rotate any KMS keys if we see anomalous usage.
nana: For communications: we should send a short advisory to affected internal teams (support + infra) and prepare a customer note if we find lateral impact. For now it's scoped to a single user.
liyah: We'll keep the user suspended for 24 hours and monitor. If no suspicious activity, restore with forced creds rotation and MFA re-enrollment.
maria: Closing interim status: containment complete (suspend + revoke + WAF blocks). Detection rule added. Follow-ups assigned. Thanks everyone. :lock::white_check_mark:
